root_cause.text: In `net/bridge/netfilter/nft_meta_bridge.c`, `nft_meta_bridge_get_eval()` copied only `ETH_ALEN` (6) bytes of `br_dev->dev_addr` into the `NFT_META_BRI_IIFHWADDR` destination, but the nftables register allocator rounded the declared 6-byte field up to an 8-byte span, leaving the last 2 bytes of the stack-backed register uninitialized and leakable.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state that `len = ETH_ALEN (6 bytes)` is rounded up to two 32-bit registers (8 bytes), while `memcpy(dest, br_dev->dev_addr, ETH_ALEN)` writes only 6 bytes; the patch fixes this by zeroing `dest[1]` before the memcpy with the comment `ETH_ALEN (6) is shorter than the destination register span (8)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero the unused bytes of the bridge MAC destination register before copying the 6-byte address.
intent_record.what: In `nft_meta_bridge_get_eval()`, immediately before copying `br_dev->dev_addr` into `dest`, the code now explicitly sets `dest[1] = 0` and adds a comment noting that `ETH_ALEN` (6) is shorter than the destination register span (8).
intent_record.how: This ensures the full destination register slot is initialized when only 6 bytes of Ethernet address data are copied, preventing stale bytes from remaining in the upper part of the 8-byte destination and making the returned value deterministic.

grouping_result.intent: Zero the unused bytes of the bridge MAC destination register before copying the 6-byte address.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it zeroes the unused padding bytes in the 8-byte register span after copying the 6-byte bridge MAC address, preventing leakage of uninitialized stack data.

candidates.rationale: This copies only 6 bytes of the bridge device MAC address into a register-sized destination that is rounded up to 8 bytes, leaving the remaining 2 bytes uninitialized and potentially leakable.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement copies only 6 bytes of the bridge MAC address into a destination that the nftables register allocator rounds up to 8 bytes, leaving the last 2 bytes of the stack-backed register uninitialized and leakable.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in this function body: for `case NFT_META_BRI_IIFHWADDR:` it does `memcpy(dest, br_dev->dev_addr, ETH_ALEN);` and then returns. The root cause states that only `ETH_ALEN` (6) bytes are copied while the nftables register allocator rounds the declared 6-byte field up to an 8-byte span, leaving 2 bytes of the stack-backed register uninitialized and leakable. This snippet also shows the corresponding init side sets `len = ETH_ALEN;`, which matches the pre-fix behavior that triggers the padding issue. There is no extra zeroing or full-span write here, so the fix is not present.

The shown code only handles bridge interface names: it selects `NFT_META_BRI_IIFNAME` / `NFT_META_BRI_OIFNAME` and then does `strncpy((char *)dest, p->br->dev->name, IFNAMSIZ);` at line 35.
